target_customer: Mid-size commercial general contractors (the company says firms doing $20M to $200M annual volume) in the U.S. and Canada
problem: Mid-market general contractors find Procore and similar tools expensive and heavy, and juggle RFIs, submittals, drawings and financials across systems.
business_model: B2B SaaS, flat fee by plan with unlimited users
product_category: Construction project management software with AI

founders.name: Emma Nazim
founders.background_notes: YC page: VP of Product at AppFolio, led AppFolio Investment Manager from 0 to 1,500 customers.

founders.name: Molly Abbott
founders.background_notes: YC page: product, operations and partnerships roles since 2010; grew up in a construction family.

founders.name: John Yoder
founders.background_notes: YC page: VP of Engineering for AppFolio Property Manager, grew the team from 65 to 250 engineers.

technical_complexity.rationale: A full construction suite (drawings, RFIs, submittals, financials, accounting sync) is broad standard engineering; the AI search and document review layers were newer in 2023.

defensibility.rationale: Project data and accounting integrations create some lock-in once a contractor runs live projects, but feature parity with Procore is a long road and pricing is the main wedge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The company itself names Procore, Autodesk and Fieldwire as the incumbents it targets; I found no source on them responding.

market_need_then: The founders say construction runs on fragmented tools and cite Procore pricing as a pain for mid-market contractors; their claims are company marketing and no dated third-party demand source was gathered.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain, contractor-friendly; leads with 'Building the next Procore' and flat pricing.

branding.brand_signature: Flat unlimited-user pricing framed against Procore

brand_strength.rationale: The company publishes comparison pages and podcast appearances, but no independent press about the brand itself was found.

outcome_analysis: Constructable is active with a small team of 6 on its YC page and keeps shipping product (an MCP server announced in 2026 on its own news page). The founders ran product and engineering at AppFolio for roughly a decade, which gives domain credibility. No verified funding, customer counts, acquisition or shutdown were found, so traction is unknown.
notes: Unverified funding figures: one newsletter says a $2.5M seed from Khosla Ventures; aggregators (VCBacked, CB Insights) list $500K pre-seed in Sept 2023 with Y Combinator and Waybury Capital. None confirmed by a second outlet, so no round is recorded. Competitors left empty: only 2026 vendor and listicle pages found. Education not found on sources opened. Completeness pass: The 500K dollar pre-seed rests on databases only (VCBacked dates it 2023-09, CB Insights lists a convertible note dated 2023-01, Employbl repeats 500K). Conflicting reports of a larger raise (a Unicorner newsletter says 2.5M dollars seed from Khosla Ventures, Caplight lists a seed dated 2024-01 with 3M dollars total) are not recorded as rounds and not summed; the gap is unresolved.
